## Global Instructions

# Unfold

Unfold turns units of work (Work Items) into pull requests that are ready for human review. Ploeg (`apps/ploeg`, Go) authorizes, budgets and executes every agent Run. The Unfold application (`apps/unfold`, TypeScript) is where people define, follow and review that work ([ADR-0002](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/adr/adr-0002-ploeg-is-the-only-engine.md)). Use the [glossary](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/reference/glossary.md) terms: a Run is one Role executing against a Work Item, and a Shift is the whole attempt.

## Commands

- Run `mise run setup` once, then run every tool through `mise exec --`.
- Run `mise run verify` before delivery. It runs every application's gates and the cross-application qualification. Live-provider tests stay opt-in.
- Run `mise run docs-check` after changing anything under `docs/` or an application's `docs/`, and `mise run agents-check` after changing anything under `.apm/`.

## Rules

- Trunk is `development`.
- Unfold depends on a released [ploeg-hq/ploeg](https://github.com/ploeg-hq/ploeg) ([ADR-0039](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/adr/adr-0039-unfold-depends-on-a-released-ploeg-through-its-contract-bundle-and-go-module.md)). `apps/ploeg` is its unpacked contract bundle; never edit it. Change Ploeg upstream.
- Unfold never executes new work types; until the engine is deleted, a managed execution never falls back to standalone.
- A deterministic demo says it is one and never invents model calls or spend.
- Keep each application's package, module, image and chart identities. [ADR-0020](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/adr/adr-0020-unfold-is-the-application-and-the-name-vloer-is-retired.md) records the one exception.
- Never change production desired state as part of a repository refactor. It lives in `webgrip/homelab-cluster`.
- Code and executable tests describe the implementation. Label proposed behavior as proposed.

## Where things live

- Rules for one directory live in `.apm/instructions/<name>.instructions.md` with an `applyTo` glob; Claude Code gets them as `.claude/rules`, the other agents in that directory's generated `AGENTS.md`. Never edit a generated `AGENTS.md`.
- Before product, pricing, portal or tenancy work, read [Who Unfold is for](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/concepts/who-unfold-is-for.md): self-hosted first, then a hosted service for agencies (system ADRs 0005–0010), none of it built yet.
- Shared guides start at [docs/index.md](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/index.md); application contracts, ADRs and research stay inside the application.
- Before changing behavior that crosses Ploeg and Unfold, read [managed execution](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/workflows/managed-execution.md).
- Before opening or reviewing a pull request, read [How work on Unfold is done](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/contributing/way-of-working.md) and the [review guide](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/contributing/review.md).
- Before adding an agent rule, skill or command, read [Agent instructions](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/contributing/agent-instructions.md) for where it belongs.

# webgrip baseline

These rules hold in every webgrip repository. The repository's own text outside this block wins where it disagrees.

- Secrets have a level, and OpenBao holds the only original ([homelab-cluster ADR-0055](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/homelab-cluster/src/branch/main/docs/techdocs/docs/adr/adr-0055-one-secrets-model-six-levels.md)). Never put a plaintext value in a file or add a `*.sops.yaml` outside the floor. Write the manifests and hand the person the `bao kv put` command; never handle the value. The `secrets-levels` skill places a secret and the `guard-secrets` hook enforces the floor.
- Follow the branching model the repository's `AGENTS.md` states; without one, commit to `main`. After a push, check the commit is on the remote (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <sha> origin/<branch>`). A forced update of a shared branch is an incident.
- Several sessions share one working tree. Commit only the paths you wrote (`git commit -- <paths>`), never `git add -A`, `git add .` or `git commit -a`, and expect any local commit to be pushed by another session at any moment ([shared working tree](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/agent-standards/src/branch/main/docs/shared-working-tree.md)).
- Run tools through mise (`mise exec -- <cmd>`); versions are pinned in `mise.toml`.
- Open a file with your file-reading tool, not `cat`, `head` or `sed` in a shell: rules scoped to a path load only when that tool reads a matching file.
- Write Conventional Commits (`feat:`, `fix:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, `refactor:`) with an optional scope, one change per commit.
- Renovate owns dependency versions: review its pull requests instead of bumping what it manages.
- Reuse before building: generate, then reference (a pinned `uses:` or an `@webgrip` package), then sync pull requests, then a one-off copy ([reuse and releases](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/agent-standards/src/branch/main/docs/reuse-and-releases.md)).
- No comments in code. Carry intent in names, types, small functions and tests; reasoning goes to `docs/` or an ADR. Machine-read directives stay: shebangs, `# syntax=`, `# renovate:`, schema hints, `@ts-*`, `eslint-*`, `# shellcheck`, `# noqa`, `//go:*` and doc comments a tool reads ([ai-skills ADR-0001](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/ai-skills/src/branch/main/org/adrs/adr-0001-no-comments-in-code.md)).
- Docs are TechDocs (MkDocs under `docs/`) and change with the behaviour. Durable knowledge goes into the repository, skill or command that owns it, never into agent memory.
- Validate with the repository's documented gate before committing, and say plainly what failed or was skipped. Check the primary source before claiming something works or never worked.
- Keep organisations apart: no names, hosts, ids or people of an employer or client in a webgrip repository.
- The Bash tool may run zsh: quote variables, use arrays, `set -o pipefail` before gating on a pipeline, and close stdin (`< /dev/null`) for CLIs that may read it.

## Files matching `.forgejo/**`

# Forgejo workflows

These workflows and actions run on Forgejo Actions, not GitHub Actions. Read [CI and release workflows](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/operations/ci.md) before changing one.

- Turn off a job that calls a reusable workflow through its `enabled` input, never with `if:`. Forgejo ignores the caller's `if:`, and a `with:` that reads a skipped job's outputs fails the whole run with no log ([why](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/docs/operations/ci.md#gating-a-reusable-workflow)).
- A workflow, action or task never prunes, mirrors or deletes refs or pushes notes; `scripts/test_release_refs.py` fails on it.

# Forgejo Actions

- Reference a reusable workflow in shorthand, pinned to a SHA: `uses: webgrip/workflows/.forgejo/workflows/<name>.yml@<sha> # vX.Y.Z`. A full `https://` URL leaves the job waiting forever for runner labels.
- An `if:` on a `uses:` job does nothing: Forgejo v15 flattens the called jobs and drops it. Gate inside the reusable workflow (`only-refs`, `enabled`) or give the calling job its own `runs-on`.
- Use `runs-on: docker`, the `Europe/Amsterdam` timezone (cron schedules too) and `@webgrip/semantic-release-config` for releases.
- Check that a GitHub Marketplace action works on forgejo-runner before proposing it ([Forgejo CI](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/agent-standards/src/branch/main/docs/forgejo-ci.md)).

## Files matching `apps/unfold/**`

# Unfold

The Unfold application is where people define, follow, steer and review the work Ploeg runs: durable operator sessions, intervention and reviewable evidence. The root `AGENTS.md` applies here too. Read [docs/architecture.md](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/apps/unfold/docs/architecture.md) and the relevant contract before a non-trivial change.

## Commands

Before delivery, run `mise run verify` from the repository root: it adds `design:check`, `icons:check`, `license:check` and the backlog check to `npm test`, which typechecks first, and `npm run check`. While iterating, `mise exec -- npm test` in this directory is the fast check. `mise run demo` starts the deterministic demo.

## Rules

- Never give an agent workspace the LiteLLM master key, Kubernetes credentials, operator session secrets or another user's credentials.
- Every mutation requires an authenticated identity and object authorization.
- Durable events survive disconnects. An intentional pause or cancel never becomes an automatic retry, and a restart never silently repeats paid work.
- Native harness session state is opaque. Portable hand-offs use repository changes and structured evidence.
- The tracker owns priority. Ploeg owns dispatch and execution.
- Never clip a label Unfold writes with an ellipsis; wrap or reword it, as [Browser UI](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/apps/unfold/docs/browser-ui.md#accessibility) explains.

## Where things live

Contracts are in `docs/contracts/`, evidence in `docs/research/`, decisions in `docs/adrs/`, deployment in `ops/`. The session-operation contract for agents is [.agents/contracts/operate-agent-session.md](https://forgejo.webgrip.dev/webgrip/unfold/src/branch/development/apps/unfold/.agents/contracts/operate-agent-session.md).
